title: `StringName` has no `operator[]` to extract single characters, like `String`
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in `v4.6.2.stable`, `v.4.7.dev5` (and likely many older versions)

### System information

Godot v4.7.dev5 - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Wed, 04 Mar 2026 18:25:08 +0000 on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6750 XT (RADV NAVI22) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600G with Radeon Graphics (12 threads) - 31.18 GiB memory

### Issue description

`StringName` does not expose an `operator[]` to index the string and obtain single chars, like `String`:
```gdscript
var str : String = "abc"
# Getter
print(str[1]) # "b"
# Setter
str[1] = "B" # "aBc"

var str_name : StringName = &"abc"
# Getter
# print(str_name[1]) # Error; cannot use subscript operator on a base of type "StringName".
```

It can be worked around by e.g. converting `StringName` to `String`, or combining `unicode_at` and `char`. But this makes for less cleaner code when compared to using `String`, and becomes a bit annoying when having to deal with internal types that are `StringName`:
```gdscript
# StringName to String
var name := String(get_child(0).name)
if name[1] == "1" or name[1] == "2":
  ...

...

# Index through `unicode_at`
var name := get_child(0).name # Node.name is a `StringName`
var character := char(name.unicode_at(1))
if character == "1" or character == "2":
  ...
```

For extracting char types only, I think it makes sense to support `operator[]` in StringName to unify behavior between `String` and `StringName`

### Steps to reproduce

N/A (detailed above in code snippets)
